newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton prices seen rising further.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton prices seen rising further.

text.p: Pakistani cotton prices are likely to rise further after sharp increases over the past few sessions amid speculation of a lower 1996/97 (July-June) crop, dealers and ginners said on Tuesday.
They said the crop may be as low as 8.5 to 9.0 million 375-lb bales, wiping out chances of exports and contrary to government estimates last month of more than 11 million bales.

"If no improvement is reported in the crop position, prices may rise to 2,600 or 2,700 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) within a few days," a former vice-chairman of Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association, Sattar Balagamwala, told Reuters.
Long-staple MNH-93 variety closed at 2,580 rupees per maund on Monday from 2,470 rupees at close of the Saturday-Thursday trading week.
Balagamwala said the latest output estimate in Punjab, the main growing province, was 6.5-6.6 million bales while Sindh province was likely to produce a bumper crop of two million.

The director of the Multan-based state-run Pakistan Cotton Research Institute, Zahoor Ahmed, said cotton production would be lower but declined to give an estimate, saying a clear picture was expected to emerge early next month.
"The crop has been damaged but we have yet to quantify the extent of the damage," he said. He said the damage was caused by excessive use of adulterated and cheap pesticides.

"We were sitting on a crop of 14 million bales in August but excessive sprays by uneducated farmers of cheap and in most cases adulterated pesticides resulted in an unusually high infestation of White Fly," he said.
In September the crop was already down to 12 million bales when dry conditions favourable to the pest worsened the situation, he added.

On October 15, the state-run Pakistan Central Cotton Committee (PCCC) put cotton output in the range of 9.5 million to 9.2 million bales, down from a target of 10 million bales and 1995/96 production of 9.96 million bales.
Balagamwala said a sharp rise in cotton prices had already wiped out exporters' profit margins and no cotton would be exported if production was down.
Exporters have registered 9,665 bales with the state-run Export Promotion Bureau up to October 22 but none has yet been shipped from this year's crop.

Pakistan exported 1.825 million bales in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June) against 230,000 bales in 1994/95 after the government lifted an export ban in February 1995. Imports from September to June 1996 were 35,960 480-lb bales.

Javed Saifullah Khan, chairman of the All Pakistan Textile Mills Association, said the crop would not be more than nine million bales and the textile industry needed at least 9.4 million bales, compared to about 8.9 million consumed last year.
